claims: Measles is a highly contagious viral respiratory disease that causes a high fever, cough, runny nose, red eyes, and a characteristic blotchy rash.
Measles is caused by the measles virus.
Measles spreads through air or direct contact with an infected person.
There is no specific antiviral treatment for measles.
Supportive care and vitamin A are recommended for measles.
Initial symptoms of measles include high fever, cough, runny nose, and red or watery eyes (conjunctivitis).
Koplik spots are small white spots that may appear inside the cheeks as early signs of measles.
A red blotchy rash appears 3-5 days after initial symptoms of measles.
The measles rash starts on the face or neck and spreads downward.
The measles rash lasts 5-6 days.
Symptoms of measles usually appear 7-14 days after exposure.
The measles virus is also known as rubeola.
Measles spreads through coughing, sneezing, and close contact.
The measles virus can live in the air or on surfaces for up to two hours.
Infected individuals can spread the measles virus from 4 days before the rash appears until 4 days after.
Measles can lead to severe health issues particularly in children under 5.
Measles can lead to severe health issues particularly in adults over 20.
Common complications of measles include ear infections.
Common complications of measles include severe diarrhea.
Pneumonia is the most common cause of death from measles.
Serious complications of measles include severe breathing problems.
Serious complications of measles include encephalitis, which is brain swelling.
Long-term complications of measles include blindness.
Measles can cause permanent brain damage in rare cases.
Measles in pregnancy increases risk of miscarriage.
Measles in pregnancy increases risk of premature birth.
Measles in pregnancy increases risk of low birth weight.
The MMR vaccine is the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine.
Two doses of the MMR vaccine are 97% effective.
Treatment for measles involves supportive care including rest, fluids, and fever reduction.
Vitamin A is recommended for children with measles.
As of March 19, 2026, there were 1,487 confirmed measles cases in the United States according to CDC 2026 data.
The 2026 U.S. measles cases were largely driven by outbreaks.
